window: Unthanksgiving Day (also known as Indigenous Peoples Sunrise Ceremony) showcases the advocacy and social justice movement for Native Americans that gained most visibility in the 1960s, including the occupation of the island of Alcatraz.

The program will include a land acknowledgement, blessing, traditional ceremony, and tribal leader presentations on Native history and the meaning of Unthanksgiving. We are honored to have leaders and community from the Muwékma Ohlone Tribe of the San Francisco Bay Area joining us again this year. We will also have tabling by MOSAIC America and the New Museum Los Gatos (NUMU).

excerpts.line: A Message from the West Valley President
window: A Message from the West Valley President
As the proud 12th President of West Valley College, I have the privilege of leading a college that is redefining what a community college can achieve.

West Valley is recognized as California’s No. 1 community college for student transfer success and by Forbes as one of the nation’s top colleges for online associate degrees. These distinctions reflect what drives our work every day: expanding opportunity, removing barriers, and creating exceptional pathways for students to transfer, launch careers, and achieve their goals.

Our momentum extends beyond the classroom. Through strong community partnerships, philanthropic support, and investments in innovative programs and student resources, we are building a college that responds to the needs of our students and the future of our region.

Dr. Jennifer Taylor-Mendoza proudly serves as the 12th president of West Valley College, breaking barriers as the first African American educator to lead the College. A visionary and trailblazer in Bay Area education, she brings over twelve years of transformative leadership within the San Mateo County Community College District. As a nationally recognized voice on educational equity, she is also the co-author of Minding the Obligation Gap in Community Colleges and Beyond: Theory and Practice in Achieving Educational Equity.

Her distinguished career includes her recent role as the President of the College of San Mateo, Vice President of Instruction at Skyline College in San Bruno, founding Dean of Academic Support and Learning Technologies at College of San Mateo (CSM), and as the Director of the Learning Center at CSM. Her unwavering commitment to academic excellence and equity continues to inspire and shape the future of higher education.
